ai.title: The contribution of Artificial Intelligence to the optimization of the supply chain with emphasis on demand forecasting and inventory management
ai.authors: Γεωργία Καλπίδη
ai.abstract: Στο σύγχρονο επιχειρηματικό περιβάλλον, η αδυναμία αξιόπιστων προβλέψεων οδηγεί συχνά είτε σε υπεραποθεματοποίηση, με αυξημένο κόστος αποθήκευσης και δέσμευση κεφαλαίων, είτε σε ελλείψεις προϊόντων, με άμεσο αντίκτυπο στο επίπεδο εξυπηρέτησης πελατών και στη φήμη της επιχείρησης, έτσι, αδιαμφησβήτητα η ακρίβεια πρόβλεψης της ζήτησης αποτελεί καθοριστικό παράγοντα επιτυχίας για τις επιχειρήσεις. Οι παραδοσιακές μέθοδοι πρόβλεψης της ζήτησης στην εφοδιαστικής αλυσίδας, όντας αρκετά περιοριστικές βασίζονται κυρίως σε στατιστικές τεχνικές και ιστορικά δεδομένα, αδυνατώντας να ενσωματώσουν αποτελεσματικά εξωτερικούς και μη γραμμικούς παράγοντες, γεγονός που σε συνδυασμό με την υποβαθμισμένη ποιότητα δεδομένων περιορίζουν τη δυνατότητα έγκαιρης λήψης αποφάσεων, δημιουργώντας αναποτελεσματικότητες σε όλο το μήκος και τα επιμέρους στάδια της εφοδιαστικής αλυσίδας. Αδιαμφησβήτητα, η Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη (ΤΝ) κατέχει καθοριστικό ρόλο στην σύγχρονη διαχείριση της εφοδιαστικής αλυσίδας. ai.title: Role of artificial intelligence and learning techniques in time series forecast of PM2.5 data: An extensive review
ai.authors: Ferdin Joe John Joseph, Sannasi Ganapathy
ai.abstract: Nowadays, this survey is necessary to equip the society with enriched Particulate Matter 2.5 (PM2.5) forecasting and enabling the health interventions with decision making policy. For researchers and academicians, this review provides an opportunity to explore the state-of-art about the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) techniques in the process of predicting the future air quality by analyzing the time series air quality data. For this purpose, the various prediction systems have been developed by various researchers in the past for predicting the various life-threatening diseases, natural calamity and air pollution by using statistical approach, ML and Deep Learning (DL) techniques. This article discusses about the various time series forecasting techniques that are developed by using Statistical approach, ML and DL Techniques. Especially, the time series forecasting methods on PM2.5 data are considered in this review by highlighting the method differences and the result comparative analysis. The PM2.5 data is widely used dataset to predict the future air pollution level in the specific regions of the world. In this review, the number of research papers published in these areas. This review shows the various experimental results of the different research works are summarized with respect to the evaluation metrics including Mean Absolute Error and…

ai.title: Utilization Of Artificial Intelligence In Demand Forecasting: A Qualitative Study Of Business Actors
ai.authors: Prendi Purba, Elfan Michael Siahaan, Charles Widianto Hulu et al.
ai.abstract: Market uncertainty in the era of volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity (VUCA) demands that businesses possess high predictive acumen. This study explores the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in demand forecasting through a descriptive qualitative approach. The study focuses on a deeper understanding of how the integration of AI technology transforms managerial decision-making processes and the dynamics of its adaptation within the digital business ecosystem in Indonesia. In-depth interviews were conducted with ten informants holding managerial and operational analyst positions in the e-commerce and technology retail sectors in Indonesia. The results show that the application of AI, particularly based on Machine Learning and Deep Learning, is able to reduce subjective human bias and capture non-linear data patterns that conventional statistical methods fail to identify. This implementation significantly improves inventory estimation accuracy, minimizes holding costs, and prevents loss of sales momentum (stockouts). However, the transition to an AI-based forecasting system faces significant structural challenges, including data quality issues (data silos), limited local talent with multidisciplinary competencies, and cultural resistance within the organization. From the perspective of managerial decision-making theory, AI acts as a cognitive amplification tool,…

ai.title: Sales Prediction Using LSTM and BiLSTM Models: A Deep Learning Approach for Time Series Forecasting
ai.authors: P.A. Arifa, Kishorkumar Devasenapathy
ai.venue: Journal of Wireless Mobile Networks Ubiquitous Computing and Dependable Applications
ai.abstract: Accurate sales forecasting significantly impacts planning strategies, inventory control, and business operations. Traditional methods of forecasting are often inadequate in recognizing intricate, multidimensional trends over time in sales data. This paper focuses on evaluating the performance of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) networks in forecasting sales time series. Due to their sophisticated nature, LSTM and BiLSTM networks are an appropriate choice for sales forecasting since they recognize sequential data patterns and long-range dependencies as well as bidirectional dependencies. This research entails the complete process of sales data from preprocessing and feature engineering to model training using LSTM and BiLSTM networks. Important evaluation metrics such as MAE, RMSE, and MAPE are used to compare the models' performances. Experimental results suggest that BiLSTM significantly outperforms LSTM in recognizing sales fluctuation patterns. This, in turn, generates more accurate forecasts. The results demonstrate the ability of deep learning techniques to improve the precision of sales forecasting and, in turn, assist companies in optimizing resource allocation and increasing profitability. Including factors such as economic indicators, industry benchmarks, and advertising would provide even more value in future model refinement.

ai.title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN COMMERCE: APPLICATIONS IN DEMAND FORECASTING AND INVENTORY MANAGEMENT
ai.authors: M. Afrabegam, A. Abinaya, M. Bavadharani et al.
ai.venue: Scholar Journal of Commerce and Management
ai.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is becoming an important component of digital transformation in commerce, particularly in activities that depend on the timely interpretation of large and changing datasets. Among these, demand forecasting and inventory management directly influence purchasing, warehousing, distribution and customer service. This paper examines how AI-supported forecasting can connect historical sales, customer behaviour, prices, promotions, seasonal effects and selected external factors with inventory decisions. Using a narrative review of concepts and applications supported by selected peer-reviewed literature on AI and supply chain management, it discusses machine learning, deep learning, time-series analysis and predictive analytics as tools for identifying demand patterns and supporting replenishment decisions. The review indicates that AI can strengthen planning by processing multiple variables at speed, identifying relationships that are difficult to detect manually and supporting more responsive inventory decisions, but it does not remove the need for managerial judgement. Forecast quality depends on the quality and relevance of data, and implementation can be constrained by cost, cybersecurity requirements, skills gaps, system integration and unexpected changes in customer behaviour. The paper therefore presents AI-enabled demand forecasting as a…

ai.title: A Review on the Implementation of Artificial Intelligence for Real-Time Product Pricing and Demand Forecasting Optimization
ai.authors: Mr. Dhananjay Nayak, Ms. Archana Thorat, Hanmant N. Renushe
ai.venue: International Journal Of Recent Advances in Engineering & Technology
ai.abstract: In the contemporary, fast-paced global market environment, organizations need to respond swiftly and effectively to changing consumer expectations, rival pricing schemes, and fluctuating economic conditions. A paradigm shift from traditional, heuristic-based approaches to data-driven, adaptive, and scalable solutions is represented by the incorporation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into pricing and demand forecasting processes. Artificial intelligence (AI) techniques, including machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and reinforcement learning (RL), have shown remarkably effective at identifying latent demand patterns, capturing non-linear relationships, and facilitating real-time dynamic pricing decisions. With a focus on their algorithmic underpinnings, implementation designs, real-world applications, and quantifiable effects on business performance, this paper summarizes the most recent state-of-the-art AI techniques used in product pricing and demand forecasting optimization.The paper also describes potential research routes and discusses current issues such data heterogeneity, model interpretability, and computational complexity. Clarifying the strategic role of AI in promoting revenue optimization, raising customer happiness, and boosting overall operational efficiency across a range of industrial areas is the key goal.

ai.title: Artificial Intelligence in Supply Chain Management: Enhancing Demand Forecasting, Inventory Optimization, and Operational Efficiency
ai.authors: Yasir Khalid, Salman Javed, Muhammad Junaid Hassan et al.
ai.venue: Journal of Business Insight and Innovation
ai.abstract: The study explored the impact of AI in Supply Chain Management, specifically on demand forecasting, inventory optimization, and operational efficiency. The data was collected using a structured questionnaire, where a quantitative cross-sectional survey design was used, with 300 professionals from the supply chain, procurement, logistics, inventory, warehousing and operations departments. The questionnaire had a 5-point Likert scale ranging from strongly disagree to strongly agree and measured the usage of Artificial Intelligence, demand forecasting, inventory optimization, and operational efficiency. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistical analysis, reliability analysis, Pearson correlation and linear regression analysis. The results showed high levels of AI utilization (M = 4.18, SD = 0.61), demand forecasting (M = 4.21, SD = 0.59), inventory optimization (M = 4.11, SD = 0.64), and operational efficiency (M = 4.23, SD = 0.58). Demand forecasting (β = .681, p < .001), Inventory optimization (β = .647, p < .001), and Operational efficiency (β = .710, p < .001) had high positive relationships with AI. The regression models accounted for 46.4%, 41.9% and 50.4% of the variance in the demand forecasting, inventory optimization and operational efficiency respectively. The results showed that the use of AI-powered technologies was linked to improved supply chain capabilities…

ai.title: Artificial intelligence and classical statistical models for time series forecasting: a comprehensive review
ai.authors: Essam Halim Houssein, Meran Mohamed, Eman M. G. Younis et al.
ai.abstract: Abstract Time series forecasting plays a critical role in decision-making across diverse domains such as finance, healthcare, and environmental monitoring. While classical statistical models like ARIMA remain interpretable and efficient, they often struggle with nonlinear patterns and dynamic dependencies. This review systematically examines how artificial intelligence (AI) and optimization techniques enhance forecasting accuracy and robustness. We evaluate modern deep learning architectures (e.g., LSTM, GRU, Transformers), hybrid frameworks (e.g., VMD-LSTM, CNN-GRU), and optimization-augmented models. A meta-analysis of over 150 studies reveals that deep learning-based approaches, particularly those enhanced with Adam and RMSProp optimizers, improve forecasting accuracy by up to 14% compared to traditional methods. Hybrid models demonstrate superior performance in multi-step predictions and handling volatility. The analysis includes financial datasets (S&P 500, NASDAQ) and environmental data (Beijing $$PM_{2.5}$$ ). Despite their power, AI-driven models face challenges including interpretability, computational cost, and data dependency. Future directions highlight explainable AI, transfer learning, and lightweight architectures to address these limitations. This work serves as a reference for researchers exploring the evolving landscape of time series forecasting through AI…

ai.title: Artificial Intelligence–Driven Demand Forecasting Models for Enhancing Supply Chain Planning Accuracy in Saudi Industrial Sectors
ai.authors: Samir Ali Syed
ai.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence Engineering and Transformation
ai.abstract: Accurate demand forecasting is a cornerstone of effective supply chain planning; however, traditional forecasting techniques often fail to capture complex market dynamics, nonlinear demand patterns, and rapid environmental changes. The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly transformed demand forecasting by enabling advanced learning from large, heterogeneous datasets through machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and hybrid analytical models. Within the context of Saudi Arabia’s industrial sectors—shaped by Vision 2030 objectives of economic diversification, industrial localization, and digital transformation—AI-driven demand forecasting presents a strategic mechanism for improving planning accuracy and operational resilience. This study examines the theoretical foundations, model architectures, implementation considerations, and strategic benefits of AI-based demand forecasting in Saudi industrial supply chains. It further discusses integration with digital platforms, real-time analytics, and multi-source data fusion. A conceptual deployment framework is proposed to demonstrate how AI forecasting can enhance planning accuracy, reduce inventory inefficiencies, and support national supply chain development goals.

ai.title: Artificial Intelligence in Supply Chain Demand Forecasting: A Structured Review of Method Evolution, Context Dependence and Research Gaps
ai.authors: Benchao Zhai
ai.venue: Advances in Economics Management and Political Sciences
ai.abstract: Demand forecasting is at the starting point of the supply chain planning link, and the forecast deviation is amplified along the chain to form a bullwhip effect, causing the backlog and shortage to occur at the same time. Machine learning and deep learning methods have entered this field in large numbers in recent years, but the literature is scattered across settings as different as retail, medicine, fresh produce and spare parts. This article is based on OpenAlex structured search to review: from 2015 to 2026, there are 2,970 records, and after qualifying the sources of journals and conferences, there are 2,227 records, of which 1,210 contain artificial intelligence method terms, and 18 representative studies are deeply synthesized. The results are threefold. The method genealogy progresses along statistical methods, tree models, deep sequence models, attention and hybrid architecture, and 91.9% of attention literature appears in 2024 and later. The statistical method has not been withdrawn. 71.9% of its literature also comes from the past three years, and it remains the main control benchmark. The accuracy advantage of artificial intelligence depends on the demand form. It is stable in continuous high-density scenarios, while the evidence in intermittent demand and truncated observation scenarios is weak. ai.title: STORE SALES PREDICTION USING MACHINE LEARNING, STATISTICAL MODELING AND DEEP LEARNING FRAMEWORKS: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS

Sales prediction involves predicting future sales of a product or service. There are several methods that businesses can use to forecast sales, including statistical analysis, market research, and expert opinion. Key factors that can impact sales predictions include market conditions, economic trends, competition, and customer behavior. However, forecasting sales can be a challenging tasks, as it require businesses to accurately forecast future demand and predict future sales in the face of changing market conditions and unpredictable customer behavior. There are also several uncertainties that businesses may face when forecasting or predicting sales, such as economic conditions, competition, customer behavior, product life cycles, and external events. In this research, we are doing sales prediction and providing a comparative analysis of three widely used techniques in the field of forecasting, namely: statistical modeling, machine learning, and deep learning. In our analysis, we are using the data given by the Rossmann supply chain, which is the second largest drugstore chain in Europe, and to the best of our knowledge, no one has ever used the deep learning approach to predict sales of these stores. ai.title: The Impact of AI On Supply Chain Planning and Demand Forecasting
ai.authors: Sachinkumar Vinodbhai Sadhu, Rajveer Singh Gohil, Dr. Hasmukh Panchal
ai.abstract: This study examines the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in improving supply chain planning and demand forecasting. With increasing market uncertainty and data complexity, traditional forecasting methods often fail to deliver accurate and timely results. AI-based techniques, especially machine learning and deep learning models, provide better prediction capabilities by analyzing large datasets and identifying hidden patterns. However, the adoption of AI in supply chains is limited due to a lack of transparency and understanding of model outputs. To address this issue, the concept of Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) is introduced, which helps decision-makers interpret and trust AI-based forecasts. The study uses a quantitative research approach based on secondary data from the FMCG sector. It highlights how AI improves forecasting accuracy, reduces inventory waste, and supports sustainable supply chain practices. The findings suggest that integrating AI with explainability can enhance decision-making, operational efficiency, and environmental performance. The study concludes by proposing a simple framework that combines AI, explainability, and sustainability for better supply chain management in emerging economies like India.

ai.title: Optimizing Demand Forecasting and Inventory Management With AI-Driven Solutions
ai.authors: K. Vijayakumar, L. A. Anto Gracious
ai.abstract: This chapter explores the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in optimizing demand forecasting and inventory management across various industries. Traditional methods, while useful, often fail to meet the demands of modern, dynamic supply chains, leading to inefficiencies such as stockouts and overstocking. AI-driven solutions, leveraging machine learning, deep learning, and predictive analytics, offer enhanced accuracy, efficiency, and cost reductions. By automating key processes and integrating with advanced technologies like IoT and blockchain, AI enables real-time decision-making and smarter resource allocation. The chapter also examines challenges in data quality, system integration, and workforce adaptation, while highlighting future research directions in AI adoption, optimization, and the integration of emerging technologies.

ai.title: Sales Forecasting Using Machine Learning
ai.authors: Shivam Agrahari
ai.venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
ai.abstract: Abstract—(1)Sales forecasting is a critical component of business strategy and inventory management, enabling organizations to make informed decisions based on future market demand. (2)This research explores the application of machine learning algorithms for improving the accuracy and efficiency of sales forecasting. (3)By analyzing historical sales data, external factors such as seasonal trends, promotions, and economic indicators, the study implements and evaluates various machine learning models including Linear Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forest, and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks. (4)The comparative analysis reveals that advanced models like LSTM outperform traditional statistical methods by capturing temporal dependencies and nonlinear patterns in the data. (5)The study also integrates data preprocessing techniques, feature engineering, and model tuning to enhance prediction performance. (6)Experimental results demonstrate that machine learning-based forecasting not only improves accuracy but also enables dynamic, real-time adaptability for businesses. (7)This work contributes to the growing body of knowledge on AI-driven decision-making, paving the way for smarter, data-informed business operations. Keywords— sales forecasting, machine learning, LSTM, time series, regression, inventory management, demand prediction, business intelligence.

ai.title: AI & demand forecasting: Systematic literature review
ai.authors: Χριστίνα Σ. Κουτσούκαλη
ai.abstract: The aim of the present thesis is a synthesis and critical evaluation of peer-reviewed evidence (2020–present) concerning artificial intelligence, machine learning, and deep learning to predict demand in the context of the supply chain and operations. Based upon a multi-database search and systematic extraction, the review maps the development of the post 2020 evidence base with regard to dominant model families and practical tooling whereby the models are tested across industries and forecasting contexts and the credibility of the reported gains in other contexts of evaluation design. In the covered studies, deep learning, particularly LSTM-family models and their hybrids, seems to be the most widespread direction of modeling, and statistical time-series baselines are a central reference point instead of being supplanted. Claims of performance are however usually conditional on evaluation decisions: time-aware validation (e.g., rolling-origin or expanding-window testing) is not universal, baseline competitiveness is not universal and lots of work is accuracy-oriented without conversion of the improvements into decision outcomes (inventory, service levels, waste). Traditional sales forecasting methods, such as time series analysis and statistical regression, are often unable to capture the complex relationships between factors influencing sales, leading to potential inaccuracies. This study aims to address these limitations by developing a sales forecasting model using deep learning and machine learning techniques. Deep learning methods, capable of modeling complex relationships and adapting to changing market conditions, are expected to improve the accuracy and cost-effectiveness of sales forecasting. This study involves data collection and preprocessing, model development and evaluation. LSTM model, performed quite well with an accuracy of approximately 80%. This study reinforces the idea that a combination of traditional forecasting methods, machine learning, and deep learning models can be utilized effectively to gain more accurate sales forecasts. ai.title: AI/ML-Based Demand Forecasting Across Industries: Transforming Traditional Sales Prediction Through Advanced Analytics
ai.authors: Balusamy Chinnappaiyan
ai.venue: Journal of Information Systems Engineering & Management
ai.abstract: Demand forecasting is a strategic discipline that anticipates future customer demand, enabling organizations to align production, inventory, and capacity decisions with market needs to drive profitability and competitive advantage. Traditional statistical methods have served organizations for decades, relying primarily on historical sales patterns and time-series analysis to generate predictions. However, contemporary business environments characterized by unprecedented demand volatility, rapidly shifting consumer preferences, and complex market dynamics have exposed significant limitations in conventional forecasting approaches. Artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies offer transformative capabilities that address these challenges through multi-source data integration, pattern recognition across vast datasets, and adaptive learning mechanisms that respond to changing market conditions in real-time. This review examines the evolution from traditional statistical forecasting to AI-powered demand prediction systems, with primary emphasis on retail sector implementations where inventory optimization and sales forecasting directly impact profitability margins. Healthcare organizations utilize similar technologies to forecast medical supply requirements and patient volume patterns, ensuring adequate resource availability while minimizing waste. Manufacturing…

ai.title: Artificial Intelligence in Mathematical Modeling of Complex Systems: A Comprehensive Review of Concepts, Applications, and Future Directions
ai.authors: Dhruvika Jadav, Tushar Mandanaka
ai.venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
ai.abstract: This paper investigates how to include artificial intelligence (AI) methods into complex system mathematical modelling. Traditionally, techniques like system dynamics, network theory, and algebraic modelling are used to study complex systems, which are distinguished by dynamic interactions, nonlinear behaviour, and high dimensionality. The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI), namely machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), has created new possibilities for improving forecast accuracy, revealing latent patterns, and allowing adaptive behaviour in these systems. Because AI algorithms are so good at learning from massive amounts of data, they may be used for time series forecasting, anomaly detection, optimisation, and decision-making. In fields like image and speech recognition, bioinformatics, and autonomous systems, neural network models—which are essential to machine learning and deep learning—have shown an amazing capacity to represent and analyse complicated phenomena. Additionally, the integration of data-driven modelling with conventional theoretical frameworks improves the capacity to capture system behaviours that are challenging to represent analytically. Complex system optimisation and self-regulation are further supported by AI-enabled adaptive control systems. ai.title: Application of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in demand forecasting in the logistics and operational activities of an enterprise
ai.authors: A. S. Gaidai, O. H. Ratushniak, A. Haiday et al.
ai.venue: Repository of Vinnytsia National Technical University (Vinnytsia National Technical University)
ai.abstract: The thesis examines modern approaches to demand forecasting in the logistics and operational activities of enterprises under conditions of digital transformation and an unstable market environment. The limitations of traditional statistical forecasting methods are substantiated, and the feasibility of using artificial intelligence and machine learning tools to improve the accuracy of managerial decision-making is proven. The study analyzes the application possibilities of ARIMA, Prophet, and XGBoost algorithms, as well as deep learning models such as LSTM, GRU, and hybrid approaches in operational planning processes.

ai.title: HaiRuo: Forecasting Ocean Eddies as Fields and Objects with a Satellite-Altimetry Foundation Model
ai.authors: Xukun Qin, Haochen Sun, Yuyang Tian et al.
ai.abstract: Mesoscale eddies carry most of the ocean's kinetic energy and move heat, salt and nutrients across basins, yet where an eddy will be two weeks ahead is still read off ocean models with post-hoc tracking heuristics. We introduce HaiRuo, which forecasts eddies as fields and as objects at once: from 30 days of satellite sea-level maps, one forward pass returns 15 days of sea level and geostrophic velocity, daily eddy masks and the trajectory of every eddy alive today. HaiRuo pairs two components with a clear division of labour: (1) HaiRuo-1B, an open-weight 1.05-billion-parameter foundation model pretrained without labels on 24 years of global satellite-altimetry observations, which supplies the 15-day physical fields and masks (+0.14 field skill and +1.1 mIoU points under the same decoder) and further lowers 15-day centre error by 1.2 km frozen (1.35 km over training from scratch); and (2) XuanJi, a Lagrangian object decoder that samples the evolving forecast in each eddy's co-moving polar frame and refines the 15-day path across three look-ahead rounds, removing 2.5 km on HaiRuo-1B (2.9 km with joint fine-tuning) and 2.5-3.3 km via its object attention across six published backbones. Under one pre-registered global evaluation over the whole ocean, HaiRuo improves on fourteen methods on every endpoint (25.2 vs. 30.6 km 15-day centre error, -18%), holding its margin outside the…

ai.title: AnchorMTS: Multi-View Signal Representation and Forecast-Anchored Fusion for Long-Term Time-Series Forecasting
ai.authors: Gao Wu, Tingting Xu, Changning Wu et al.
ai.abstract: Long-term time-series forecasters typically optimize a single numerical representation, even though the same history exposes complementary geometry, recurrence, and semantic structure. We propose AnchorMTS, which derives self-aligned visual and textual views from each observed window and uses them only to refine a complete numerical forecast. A trainable evidence path produces a candidate forecast, while a parameter-free output projection enforces an exact per-variable bound on its displacement from the numerical anchor. Across six benchmarks and four horizons, AnchorMTS achieves the best macro MSE/MAE (0.336/0.367) among seven supervised baselines and wins 18 of 24 MSE settings against the cellwise baseline envelope; removing the auxiliary path raises macro MSE to 0.340. The projection leaves 95.8% of candidate refinements unchanged while yielding zero bound violations, showing that complementary multi-view evidence can improve forecasting while its final influence remains explicitly controlled.

ai.title: Learning Evidence-Grounded Reasoning for Context-Aware Time Series Forecasting
ai.authors: Xingpeng Gao, Mingyue Cheng, Daoyu Wang et al.
ai.abstract: LLM-driven time series forecasting has become increasingly promising by leveraging contextual features to generate future values directly or refine forecast priors. However, incorporating contextual features alone does not ensure that models can identify which features matter for forecasting and understand what they suggest about future dynamics. We argue that the fundamental challenge is how to extract predictive evidence from contextual features and when and how to leverage it to guide forecasting decisions. In this paper, we propose CastReasoner, an evidence-grounded reasoning model for context-aware time series forecasting. Specifically, CastReasoner uses a structured chain of thought (CoT) to extract predictive evidence from contextual features, infer the future dynamics suggested by this evidence, and assess these dynamics against the forecast prior to guide adaptive forecasting decisions. To enable this capability, we design a reasoning-centric two-stage post-training framework including supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL). First, we synthesize reasoning trajectories through controllable multi-teacher guidance and select high-quality ones using a novel student-aware difficulty metric. ai.title: Do Time-Series Foundation Models Forecast Index-Futures Returns? A Preregistered Evaluation of Models, Metrics, and Input Representations
ai.authors: Rishabh Upadhyay
ai.abstract: We ask whether the apparent forecasting skill of frozen time-series foundation models (TSFMs) on intraday index-futures returns is incremental skill. In a pre-registered evaluation on E-mini Nasdaq-100 (NQ) and E-mini S&P 500 (ES) futures, a common panel of five zero-shot models (Chronos-Bolt, Chronos-2, TimesFM 2.5, Moirai 2.0 and TiRex), plus separate experiments with Kronos, is compared with a no-change forecast at 5-120 minutes, using native prices, log returns, volatility-standardised returns and a volume clock as inputs. On a blind set opened once, 0 of 160 model-representation-horizon-market cells beat no-change, and a Hansen SPA test gives p = 1.000 on both markets; a later retrospective hold-out, scored as a descriptive check, gives 0 of 120. Input representations change forecast magnitude but not accuracy, and a transformation-aware ridge regression does as well. Several standard measures nevertheless suggest skill. Price-level correlation exceeds 0.9996, but no-change scores higher. Within-day RankIC across forecast origins rewards a trivial revert-to-mean rule (+0.35 at 30 minutes); we derive the expected within-day covariance under a random walk in closed form, and a sign-randomised null reproduces about 95% of the observed value. ai.title: Forecast Value Add: Reward-Based Action Selection over Probabilistic Demand Forecasts
ai.authors: Ankur Verma
ai.abstract: Strong machine-learning ensembles capture much of the trend, seasonality, and known events in demand, yet they can still understate peaks, miss moving events, or mistake temporary changes for shifts in demand level. We address this gap by framing forecast refinement as a reward-driven decision problem. For each forecast period, we let an agent choose among values already produced by the ensemble: its base forecast, distribution-free bounds, quantiles, and a bias-corrected estimate. We evaluate these choices against context-matched historical periods, accounting for calendar position, recurring and moving events, trend, price, and promotions. We then apply a structural seasonal guard to constrain adjustments and record the model, agent, and planner contributions to every published value. We evaluate our approach across five retail, consumer-goods, and direct-to-consumer deployments over nine months. Our refined forecasts reduce mean WMAPE by 6.3% compared with the stacked machine-learning forecast for every customer, with gains reaching 16.7%, and achieve the lowest error in 35 of 45 customer-months. Compared with statistical forecasts, our approach reduces mean error by 18.7%. These results demonstrate that context-aware, auditable action selection can add forecast value beyond a strong ensemble.

ai.title: Conformal Prediction for Multi-Step Forecasting: Conditional Coverage and Sharp Score Calibration Rates
ai.authors: Siyuan He, Yuhong Yang
ai.abstract: Uncertainty quantification in prediction is a central problem in statistics and machine learning. Conformal prediction provides a flexible approach to constructing prediction sets with valid marginal coverage under exchangeability. In this paper, we investigate conformal prediction for both one-step and multi-step forecasting from a single stationary time series, addressing temporal dependence and the additional challenges of joint prediction across multiple horizons. We propose a kernel-based framework, called Time series Residual Analysis for Calibration with Kernels (TRACK), for estimating conditional quantiles of residual scores and constructing prediction sets from rolling-window forecasters. The framework accommodates heterogeneous uncertainty across horizons and accounts for dependence induced by rolling estimation, while allowing predictor memory and forecast horizons to grow with the sample size. Our finite-sample bounds quantify how temporal dependence and overlapping score windows affect calibration and coverage. We further derive bounds for conditional quantile estimation and pointwise conditional coverage discrepancy. The guarantees extend to more general predictors that admit an accurate rolling-window approximation. ai.title: Means vs. Foundation Models for Emergency Call Forecasting
ai.authors: Feriel Fass, Djemel Ziou, Marie-Flavie Auclair-Fortier
ai.abstract: This study investigates whether generalized means can achieve forecasting performance comparable to that of TimeGPT for daily emergency call volume prediction. Specifically, two families of generalized means, the Hölder means (HM) and the Lehmer means (LM), are evaluated against fine-tuned TimeGPT across forecasting horizons ranging from one to seven days. Forecasting performance is assessed on a real-world emergency call dataset using multiple error metrics, and Diebold-Mariano test. Experimental results show that HM and LM achieve nearly identical predictive performance across all forecasting horizons. For short-term forecasting, both generalized means outperform TimeGPT, with reductions of mean absolute error (MAE) approximately 1.24\% and 2.48\% at horizons of one and three days, respectively. Conversely, TimeGPT achieves a lower error at the seven-day horizon, with an descresing of MAE by 1.98\%. However, Diebold-Mariano tests reveal no statistically significant differences between the methods at the evaluated horizons. These findings suggest that generalized means can provide competitive forecasting performance compared with a energyvore foundation model.

ai.title: Daily Emergency Call Volume Forecasting using Univariate and Multivariate TimeGPT
ai.authors: Feriel Fass, Djemel Ziou
ai.abstract: This study investigates the potential of TimeGPT, a pretrained foundation model for timeseries, for forecasting daily emergency call volumes. Real-world emergency call data, comprising 2,101 daily observations, are used to evaluate both univariate and multivariate forecasting settings under one-step-ahead and seven-day multi-step-ahead scenarios. The multivariate forecasting incorporates temporal, meteorological, demographic, and socioeconomic variables. A chronological training, validation, and test split is adopted to prevent information leakage, while hyperparameters are selected using the validation set through grid search and early stopping when applicable. Forecasting performance is evaluated using multiple error metrics. Its forecasting performance is compared with several established forecasting approaches, including Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous Regressors (SARIMAX), Poisson regression (PR), Negative Binomial regression (NBR), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). ai.title: ClusLoad: Cluster-Guided Model Sharing for Scalable Distribution Transformer Load Forecasting
ai.authors: Fangzhou Lin, Guoshun He, Yi Wang et al.
ai.abstract: Large-scale device-level load forecasting for distribution transformers is challenged by substantial cross-device heterogeneity and the deployment burden of maintaining device-specific forecasting models. Existing approaches typically rely either on device-specific models, which are difficult to scale to large transformer populations, or on global models, which reduce deployment complexity but may overlook heterogeneous load patterns across devices. To address this trade-off, this study develops a trend-clustered forecasting framework that enables model sharing among transformers with similar temporal behaviors. Representation Learning for Time Series using Time-Embeddings (T-Rep) is employed to learn compact temporal representations of transformer load series, which are subsequently grouped using a Gaussian mixture model (GMM). Representative transformers are sampled within each cluster to train cluster-specific Patch Time Series Transformer (PatchTST) models while retaining device-level predictions. The framework is evaluated using real-world 15-min operational data from nearly one thousand distribution transformers. The proposed framework reduces mean absolute error (MAE) by approximately 20% relative to the direct PatchTST baseline, achieves a high-load warning accuracy of 95.66%, while requiring only seven cluster-specific forecasting models. ai.title: StatPrompt-LLM: A Lightweight Statistical Refinement for Foundation-Style Time-Series Forecasting
ai.authors: Aniket Sinha, Veronica W. Tsou
ai.abstract: Time-series forecasting has recently seen a paradigm shift with the introduction of foundation-style models that adapt large pretrained language architectures to sequential data. However, effectively exposing fundamental temporal structures, such as trend, scale, and temporal dependence, to these models remains an open challenge, particularly when the available observations are limited. In this paper, we conduct an exploratory empirical study across different generations of forecasting architectures and propose StatPrompt-LLM, a lightweight statistical refinement of Time-LLM. StatPrompt-LLM augments the existing Time-LLM prompting mechanism with dataset-level statistical information and introduces a zero-initialised autoregressive bypass as a complementary linear forecasting pathway. We evaluate our framework on electricity and meteorological time-series benchmarks, including ETTh1, ETTh2, and Weather, under full-prefix and reduced-prefix configurations. Under the 10% reduced-prefix configuration, StatPrompt-LLM achieved lower in-sample prediction errors than Time-LLM, with unweighted average relative reductions across datasets of 40.2% in MSE and 21.4% in MAE. Full-prefix results were more dataset-dependent. ai.title: SWXAI: A Unified Multimodal Explainability Library for Space Weather Forecasting and Heliophysics
ai.authors: Benedict Antonio Mervyn, Anli Ji, Manolis K. Georgoulis et al.
ai.abstract: Space weather forecasting and heliophysics increasingly rely on machine learning models that process heterogeneous inputs such as multi-viewpoint multi-wavelength solar images and rasters, multivariate time series, spatial annotations, and tabular event-level data. However, explainability workflows remain fragmented across libraries, model interfaces, and output formats, limiting reuse and reproducibility. We present SWXAI, an open-source library that unifies explainable AI (XAI) workflows for image, time-series, and tabular data in space weather forecasting and heliophysics. SWXAI provides a common, extensible interface across commonly used vision, time-series, and tabular learning models, with validation, adaptation, and persistent explanation objects. It also includes domain-grounded examples, reproducible notebooks, tests, and documentation, enabling users to inspect outputs, swap models or explainers, and extend workflows to new heliophysics datasets. SWXAI reduces modality-specific engineering overhead and supports comparable, reusable explanations across heterogeneous scientific machine learning pipelines. A benchmark against direct backend implementations shows that SWXAI substantially reduces the code users write to produce an explanation, with no practical runtime cost.

logistics.abstract: Rapid advances in digitalization have brought about a radical transformation in the retail sector, accelerating the transition from traditional to online retail. Shifts in customer habits, particularly following the Covid-19 pandemic, have led to significant increases in e-commerce volume. This rapid growth in online sales has intensified competition, requiring businesses to respond more quickly to changing customer expectations. In this context, the importance of modern logistics management in online retail is increasing, and business processes are being enhanced with digital solutions. logistics.title: The Supply Chain Management Team
logistics.authors: Helene S. York
logistics.abstract: This chapter delves into the organizational structure of the supply chain management (SCM) team. It outlines the key functions that comprise this critical department, many of which have evolved from previously siloed roles in operations and finance. These core functions include procurement (vendor selection and tendering), contract negotiation, demand forecasting, contract management, purchasing, and logistics management. The chapter explores the primary goals of these teams, with a significant focus on vendor selection criteria such as ensuring consistent supply, quality, and cost, as well as the crucial aspect of de-risking the supply chain. The concept of controlled spend as a key metric for organizational visibility and integrity is introduced. The chapter touches upon broader SCM goals related to delivery performance, inventory management, cost reduction, and the integration of sustainability goals. By providing a clear understanding of the structure, functions, and objectives of the SCM team, this chapter offers valuable insights for anyone seeking to optimize their organization's supply chain operations to achieve strategic alignment.

logistics.abstract: Global supply chains rely on the interactions of thousands of heterogeneous agents, posing significant challenges for optimization. While traditional optimization often assumes homogeneity to ensure tractability, Reinforcement Learning struggles with sample inefficiency when scaling to high-dimensional state spaces. We propose a Differentiable Agent-Based Model for multi-echelon inventory management. Furthermore, we utilize gradient sensitivity analysis to generate causal heatmaps, accurately recovering inherent lead-time delays from the computation graph. This approach bridges the gap between simulation and optimization, enabling the efficient training of self-correcting Digital Twins.

logistics.abstract: E-commerce supply chains generate large volumes of customer feedback and operational data that remain underutilized in inventory management. Traditional inventory classification techniques such as ABC analysis rely primarily on annual dollar usage, while multi-criteria inventory classification (MCIC) methods extend this but still depend on structured quantitative data and do not utilize unstructured information available in modern supply chains. This paper proposes an LLM-based feature extraction approach that transforms unstructured sources such as customer reviews into quantitative features using vector embeddings and LLM-generated evaluation criteria. The enriched feature set is incorporated into an MCIC framework based on the Hadi-Vencheh model. Experimental results show measurable reclassification effects when customer sentiment signals are included, demonstrating that integrating unstructured data into MCIC can enhance inventory prioritization.

logistics.title: Cross-Border Ownership and Input Access: Evidence from the Lithium Supply Chain
logistics.authors: Kei Irizawa
logistics.abstract: How does cross-border ownership shape the lithium supply chain? Using global data on mines and refineries, I estimate a model in which ownership can lower refiners' effective ore costs, encourage mines to restrict spot sales, and soften competition. To study these effects, I examine policies motivated by national security concerns about reliable access to critical mineral inputs: divestiture of Chinese stakes in overseas producers and a ban on ore exports to China. Divestiture increases spot ore supply but leaves lithium output nearly unchanged, while continued trade preserves Chinese access to ore. The export ban reduces global lithium supply because refining capacity elsewhere cannot fully replace lost Chinese production. Ownership transfers do not reserve ore for domestic production; restricting Chinese access imposes a substantial supply cost at existing capacities.

logistics.title: Distributionally Robust Dynamic Inventory Control: Automatic Recovery under Martingale Demand
logistics.authors: Jianzhi Leng, Daniel Zhuoyu Long, Lun Ran et al.
logistics.abstract: Problem definition: We study dynamic inventory control for battery-swapping stations that combine central replenishment with automatic local recovery. Central replenishment improves immediate battery availability but reduces the depleted-battery pool available for subsequent recovery, creating an intertemporal trade-off. Managing this trade-off is particularly challenging when historical demand data are limited and future demand is uncertain and temporally dependent. Methodology/results: We develop a time-consistent distributionally robust dynamic program under martingale demand ambiguity, using the latest observed demand as the next conditional mean without requiring a fully specified demand distribution. We establish an optimal order-up-to policy for every finite horizon and identify two critical recovery rates governing replenishment decisions. Under a regular penalty condition, we derive explicit finite-horizon policies and worst-case demand distributions, showing that sufficiently strong automatic recovery makes central replenishment unnecessary in nonterminal periods. Extensions to submartingale and supermartingale demand reveal contrasting behaviors, including eventual full-capacity replenishment under upward ambiguity and recovery-induced positive replenishment under downward ambiguity. Managerial implications: Numerical experiments demonstrate that the robust policy…

logistics.title: Palimpsestic Accountability in the US Federal AI Inventories
logistics.authors: Dipto Das, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed, Aditya Vashistha et al.
logistics.abstract: An AI inventory is a structured, often public record in which a government or organization lists and describes the AI systems it uses or plans to use. Studies of single AI inventory releases describe what systems do but say little about how they are governed over time. We linked entries across three releases of the US Federal AI Use Case Inventory (2023--2025), compared answers only where both releases required them, and analyzed governance accounts through a dual deductive-inductive approach, guided by the Algorithmic Decision-Making Adapted for the Public Sector (ADMAPS) framework. As the inventory grew from 710 to 3,611 entries from 2023 to 2025, fewer required answers were left blank, but accountability was rewritten through three mechanisms. Each release \emph{redrew} the scope of the questions; agency-assigned classifications \emph{gated} what was reported; and answers were also \emph{overwritten}, with gains and losses concentrated in single agencies and little account of human oversight and judgment. These findings show that each release redraws the boundary of accountability and leaves the public to \emph{re-stitch} the records, a condition we term \textbf{palimpsestic accountability}. We recommend versioned records, reasons for every reclassification, public files that distinguish kinds of missing answers, and oversight documented as conditions to improve public…

logistics.title: Late Autumn: LLM Agents Specialize a General Multi-Robot Planner for One Warehouse
logistics.authors: Yimin Tang, Han Zhang, Shao-Hung Chan et al.
logistics.abstract: No algorithm is best on all problems, but a real warehouse is a narrow problem: its layout and processes rarely change. Operators still run one general multi-robot planner at many sites, because experts cannot tune it for each one. In this work, which we call Late Autumn, we explore whether LLM coding agents running autonomous research can specialize a general planner for one site, trading generality for throughput, much as post-training adapts a pretrained LLM to one task. We study six campaigns on a lifelong planner that combines task assignment with multi-agent path finding, on a floor modeled on an existing automated warehouse. We find that (1) the agents raise throughput by 22--60%, and the gains hold on unseen seeds; (2) they rediscover known MAPF mechanisms, such as corridor-exit priorities, local guidance, and rollouts, and independent campaigns find the same bottleneck; (3) the gains largely carry over to another layout, a larger fleet, and other service times, shrink with a smaller fleet, and mostly vanish under an outbound-heavy demand mix; and (4) each final patch (0.7k--2.4k lines) is a chain of scored commits with a median step of 27 lines, so experts can review it, and review finds problems that the score misses; some patches multiply planner compute by over 100x. LLM agents can therefore turn each site's bias into extra throughput at little engineering cost,…

logistics.title: Halal-NeSyNet: Clause-Scoped Neuro-Symbolic Cross-Attention for Automated Food Ingredient Auditing and Risk-Aware Halal Logistics Triage
logistics.authors: Mochamad Rizal Fauzan, Naila Nursyifa, Irgi Surya
logistics.abstract: Verifying that a packaged food is Halal requires reading ingredient declarations and E-number additives before goods enter certified warehouses. Dual-origin additives such as E471, E422, E441 and E920 are Mushbooh (doubtful) unless a botanical, microbial or certified-Halal qualifier appears in the same ingredient clause, so a plant-based qualifier on one clause must not clear an unqualified additive in another. We call a failure to respect this scope cross-clause modifier confounding and build a benchmark of 3,199 items (277 Open Food Facts records and 2,922 template-generated clause-swap items, labelled by an explicit 50-code rule base rather than by a certification authority) with a 540-item counterfactual suite. We propose Halal-NeSyNet, which couples a DistilBERT encoder with a 16-dimensional rule-derived symbolic vector through cross-attention and gated fusion, trained with an asymmetric false-Halal risk loss. Over five seeds, text-only TF-IDF baselines reach 86.25-86.71 % accuracy with 13.42-21.73 % false-Halal leakage and 6.33-26.00 % counterfactual triad consistency, whereas Halal-NeSyNet reaches 97.04+/-0.34 % and 99.67+/-0.50 %. Gradient boosting given the same symbolic vector reaches 96.25+/-1.24 % (+0.59 points from Halal-NeSyNet, 95 % CI [-1.11, +2.28]), so most of the gain comes from clause-scoped symbolic features and not from the network, and the risk loss did…

logistics.title: Improved Approximation Guarantees for Periodic-Review Stochastic Inventory Control
logistics.authors: Danny Segev
logistics.abstract: In periodic-review stochastic inventory control, replenishment policies must balance holding and backlogging costs while responding to uncertain demands and evolving forecasts that may be arbitrarily correlated and nonstationary. In this general information setting, Levi, P{á}l, Roundy, and Shmoys (Mathematics of Operations Research 2007) established that the fully adaptive optimum can be approximated within factor $2$, which had remained the best-known performance guarantee since then. Their marginal cost accounting and dual-balancing framework made this comparison possible without computing optimal decisions across future trajectories, opening a broad research program on approximation algorithms for stochastic inventory systems. We break this long-standing barrier for periodic-review stochastic inventory control, showing how to compete against the fully adaptive benchmark within factor $\frac{ e }{ e-1 } \approx 1.582$ while retaining general demand correlations and evolving forecasts. We attain these advances by discovering a structural connection between marginal inventory accounting and weighted stopping problems, where each unit's conditional holding charge forms a supermartingale, while postponing its order incurs a history-dependent backlog charge. To leverage the random thresholding approach of Ma and Tzamos (ICML 2023) in this context, we develop a potential-function…

logistics.title: Quantum Vehicle Routing Problem: a smart initialization strategy for ill-conditioned optimization landscapes
logistics.authors: Emanuele Casciaro, Mario De Simone, Stefano Martina et al.
logistics.abstract: With the expansion of complex transport infrastructure, new paths for linking different destinations have emerged, allowing the definition of multiple routes. The introduction of new roads may also lead to disruptions in traffic flow. This problem can be generalized into a special case of VRP, which aims to find the optimal route for a fleet of vehicles within a network of destinations. Finding solutions to this problem requires an exponential number of operations, hindering the ability of exact solvers to deal with large instances, which must therefore be tackled using heuristics, often leading to suboptimal results. Quantum-based algorithms may allow us to find exact solutions in polynomial time with high probability, offering a potential future alternative to classical solvers and in this work, we focus on the QAOA. Our novel contributions are a parameter-initialization strategy that improves the convergence probability and the integration of the subtour constraints directly into the optimization without using additional qubits by employing an approximation of exponential equality constraints. We believe that our results pave the way for effectively solving instances of VRP using quantum-based solutions, leveraging the space-efficient problem encoding and our initialization strategy, which limits the effect of barren-plateau under random parameter initialization.

logistics.title: Carbon-Aware Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Decision-Focused Learning
logistics.authors: Jaume Reixach, Wanru Chen, Jiaming Wu et al.
logistics.abstract: Electric vehicles produce no tailpipe emissions, but charging them produces emissions that depend on the time-varying generation mix of the electricity consumed. We study an Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with a carbon-aware objective that accounts for charging-related emissions alongside conventional routing costs. The problem determines routing, charging, and waiting decisions, allowing charging demand to be shifted toward periods with lower grid carbon intensity. Because these decisions depend on forecasts of future carbon intensity, we propose a decision-focused learning approach so that the training of the model employed for predicting the carbon intensity of the grid over time is solver-aware. In particular, we train a linear predictor using approximate SPO+ directions and employ a time-limited Large Neighborhood Search followed by exact postprocessing as the underlying solver. Experiments on realistic Germany-based instances show that explicitly considering charging-related emissions reduces realized emissions by 28.76% on average relative to carbon-blind optimization, although at the expense of higher non-carbon operating cost. Moreover, decision-focused training reduces realized total cost by 2.30% on average relative to conventional prediction-focused learning and performs better on 75.5% of the test instances, despite substantially lower pointwise predictive…

logistics.title: DEG: Diffusion-Enhanced GFlowNet for Solving Vehicle Routing Problems
logistics.authors: Ni Zhang, Zhiqin Zhang, Ling Pan et al.
logistics.abstract: Traditional neural solvers for solving vehicle routing problems (VRPs) often suffer from limited solution diversity, motivating the development of Generative Flow Network (GFlowNet)-based models. However, the effectiveness of these models is frequently constrained by insufficient flow expansion in high-reward regions, limiting their ability to distribute probability across promising solution routes. Deeper exploration could yield superior results. Diffusion models, in contrast, provide stronger structural guidance for exploration. These two paradigms are naturally complementary: GFlowNet can supply edge-level signals for diffusion to embed, while diffusion can guide broader exploration. Leveraging this synergy, we propose Diffusion-Enhanced GFlowNet (DEG), a novel framework that integrates GFlowNet with a diffusion model to encourage richer flow expansion toward high-reward regions and derive higher-quality solutions. Specifically, DEG exploits GFlowNet's inherent diversity to generate edge-specific backward signals, applies the stochastic noise schedule of diffusion to perturb these signals, and then denoises them within the GFlowNet paradigm. To further improve scalability, we introduce a specialized decoder capable of dynamically adapting to diverse problem scales. Extensive experimental evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets, including instances with up to 10,000…

sales.title: Artificial Intelligence in B2B sales: Transforming customer interaction, B2B sales strategy, and the role of the B2B salesperson
sales.abstract: This thesis examines how artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming B2B sales, with a focus on efficiency, customer engagement, and the evolving role of the salesperson. The study aims to understand how AI tools are used in practice and how they influence sales processes and professional roles. The research was conducted using a qualitative approach, based on semi-structured interviews with professionals working in B2B sales and business development. The collected data was analyzed to identify key themes related to the use of AI in sales environments. The findings indicate that AI is widely used to automate routine tasks, support decision-making, and enhance customer personalization. Rather than replacing sales professionals, AI is transforming their role by enabling them to focus on more strategic and relationship-driven activities. The study concludes that the future of B2B sales lies in combining AI-driven insights with human expertise to create value and maintain strong customer relationships.

sales.title: An Essay on the Evolving Role of B2B Salespeople in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Challenges and Opportunities.
sales.venue: International Journal of Marketing Communication and New Media
sales.abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence in B2B sales is transforming processes, enhancing customer experiences, and reshaping sales roles. This essay examines AI’s impact, highlighting its benefits in efficiency, automation, and data-driven decision-making while addressing challenges such as cultural resistance and skill development. A conceptual model outlines key dimensions of AI-driven sales transformation. The study concludes that the future lies in a "Hybrid Model", where AI and human expertise coexist for innovation and competitive advantage. This essay can serve as a basis for future studies by proposing the conceptual model and suggesting empirical approaches to assess the impacts of AI on salespeople's performance. sales.title: AI-enabled social media: implications for salespeople, sales leadership, and sales organizations
sales.authors: Vishag A. Badrinarayanan, Christine Lai-Bennejean, Adam A. Rapp et al.
sales.venue: Journal of Personal Selling and Sales Management
sales.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded within social media, AI-enabled social media is increasingly changing how salespeople, sales leaders, and sales organizations engage with customers, partners, and internal stakeholders. Yet, sales research has largely focused on how sales actors use traditional social media with little emphasis on the implications of AI, a notable gap that also remains in the rapidly evolving research on AI in B2B sales. Thus, there is limited understanding of how embedding AI within social media alters the action possibilities available to sales actors. Drawing on affordance theory, we define AI-enabled social media and examine how AI alters and extends traditional social media affordances across external social media and enterprise social media (ESM), with implications for salespeople across the sales process, sales leadership across key leadership roles, and sales organizations across key organizational domains. We then discuss theoretical and managerial implications and develop a research agenda for advancing knowledge of AI-enabled social media in B2B sales.

sales.title: Penerapan Artificial Intelligence dalam Meningkatkan Penjualan B2B (Business To Business)
sales.abstract: This study aims to deeply examine the role and impact of AI implementation in the B2B sales process, including implementation challenges. The method used is a qualitative approach with descriptive studies, through a literature review of scientific journals, industry reports, and relevant previous studies. The analysis results show that the application of AI in B2B sales not only improves the accuracy of marketing strategies and lead conversion, but also strengthens the concept of value co-creation through collaboration between salespeople and AI systems. Technologies such as machine learning, predictive analytics, and NLP-based chatbots have been proven to accelerate sales cycles, expand service reach, and increase productivity by up to 30%. However, implementation challenges remain, including limited digital infrastructure, a lack of competent human resources, and organizational resistance to technological transformation. Therefore, optimal AI integration requires institutional readiness, adaptive strategies, and continuous investment in technology and human resource development. These findings provide theoretical and practical contributions to the development of AI-based B2B sales strategies, particularly in the context of the digital industry in Indonesia. Furthermore, the application of AI in B2B sales also opens up new opportunities for service personalization. With the…

sales.title: How AI Can Automate the Sales Process for Lower-Level Managers in the B2B Landscape

sales.title: Digital Transformation of B2B Sales Processes: Exploring Technology Adoption and Sales Performance Through a Qualitative Study
sales.abstract: Digital transformation is reshaping business-to-business (B2B) sales processes through the growing use of customer relationship management systems, analytics dashboards, automation tools, digital communication channels, and predictive technologies. However, the performance effects of these tools remain insufficiently understood, particularly in complex B2B sales contexts where commercial work is relational, knowledge-intensive, and strongly dependent on organizational routines. Drawing on the Technology Acceptance Model, this study explores how B2B sales actors perceive, adopt, resist, and integrate digital tools into their daily commercial practices. Based on 18 semi-structured interviews with sales directors, sales managers, business development managers, and senior sales representatives, the study identifies a conditional process linking digital tool adoption to perceived sales performance. The findings show that adoption is mainly driven by perceived usefulness, while perceived ease of use depends less on interface simplicity than on compatibility with sales routines. Resistance emerges when tools create administrative duplication, threaten commercial autonomy, or remain poorly integrated into existing workflows. The study further shows that digital tools improve perceived sales performance indirectly, mainly through CRM integration, shared customer memory, data-driven…

sales.title: Artificial intelligence in business-to-business sales : examining risks, challenges, and negative implications across the sales process
sales.abstract: This thesis aims to investigate the possible risks, challenges and negative effects of utilizing AI within B2B sales at all levels of the sales process. Although AI has been widely implemented to increase operational efficiency and provide assistance for decision-making, this study will focus on the ways in which AI affects human judgment and potentially causes unintended consequences. This research followed a qualitative exploratory research approach based on semi structured interviews. Data from the study was gathered through thirteen interviews with individuals who worked in B2B sales roles. An abductive methodology was used to connect the empirical findings with the previous theories. Thematic analysis was used to analyze the interview data. The study found that human judgment continues to play an important role in evaluating and verifying the output from AI. As such, sales professionals are able to proactively manage risk through the review of AI-generated content, selective usage of AI and gradual integration of AI into their existing workflow. Ultimately the study highlights that the technological impacts of AI in B2B sales are not solely technical in nature, they are also influenced by how individuals utilize and engage with technology in practice.

sales.title: Tekoälyn hyödyntäminen B2B -myynnissä

Tutkimuksessa tarkasteltiin erityisesti tekoälyn hyödyntämistä B2B-myynnin myyntiprosessin eri vaiheissa sekä tekijöitä, jotka edistävät tai estävät tekoälyn tehokasta käyttöä B2B-myyntiorganisaatioissa. Opinnäytetyön tavoitteena on lisätä ymmärrystä tekoälyn roolista osana B2B-myyntiprosessia. Työ toteutettiin sekä, kvalitatiivisena- että kvantitatiivisena tutkimuksena. Työn aineisto hankittiin teema- ja kyselyhaastatteluilla B2B-myynnin parissa työskenteleviltä asiantuntijoilta. Haastatteluaineisto analysoitiin laadullisen sisällönanalyysin ja teemoittelun avulla. sales.title: Managing the burnout process over time: A within-person examination of salesperson burnout
sales.authors: Dayle R. N. Childs, Belinda Dewsnap, Alec Pappas et al.
sales.abstract: Burnout is highly prevalent in the sales force, and is a serious concern for sales managers. Salesperson burnout is a process that requires management over time, yet no longitudinal within-person evidence exists regarding how salesperson burnout evolves over time or how to best manage the process. Using a 4-month repeated measures study of 171 B2B salespeople, we present the first longitudinal evidence of the within-person salesperson burnout process, and examine how key sales manager and salesperson variables can shape this process as it evolves. Results show some support for the burnout process, but find no link between diminished personal accomplishment and depersonalization. Moreover, positive feedback plays no role in mitigating burnout's evolution, while active coping and negative feedback mitigate the impacts of diminished personal accomplishment and depersonalization on emotional exhaustion, respectively. Our work presents tangible interventions that can help to reduce burnout as it evolves within salespeople over time.

sales.title: Emotional Intelligence Abilities and Work Engagement among Salespersons: A Conservation of Resources Theory Perspective from Germany’s Pharmaceutical Industry
sales.authors: Yahya Awadh Al-Nami, Amiya Bahaumik, Akram Mufareh Alshammakh
sales.venue: Journal of Business and Management Studies
sales.abstract: Sustaining salespersons’ work engagement has become a critical concern amid intensifying professional demands and increasing turnover within the German pharmaceutical B2B sector. Guided by the Conservation of Resources (COR) theory, this study examines how four distinct abilities of emotional intelligence—self-emotion appraisal, others’ emotion appraisal, emotion utilization, and emotion regulation—affect salespersons’ work engagement. Employing a quantitative design, data were collected from 340 pharmaceutical sales representatives in North Rhine-Westphalia and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The results reveal that all four emotional intelligence abilities exert significant positive effects on work engagement, confirming the hypothesized relationships. Among these, the utilization and regulation of emotion emerged as the most influential predictors, underscoring their pivotal role in sustaining engagement within emotionally demanding sales environments. Overall, the four abilities of EI explained 68% of the variance in work engagement, affirming its value as a psychological resource that enhances motivational energy and mitigates emotional strain. sales.title: Beyond Use Cases: A Strategic Framework for Scaling AI in B2B Sales
sales.abstract: Even though early AI adoption is underway, many B2B sales organizations are finding it difficult to scale beyond isolated pilots. More organizations are now reporting failed AI initiatives. The unique complexities in B2B sales make this challenge even more acute: multistakeholder landscape, long decision cycles and offerings that often require customization. The key to realizing the full value of AI in B2B sales is a holistic, intentional approach to its deployment. This article introduces a practical framework for enterprise leaders to deploy and scale AI in B2B sales.

sales.title: Automaatiojärjestelmät yritysmyynnin tukena
sales.abstract: This bachelor's thesis examines the utilization of automation systems in B2B-sales and their applications in the sales process. The objective of this thesis was to identify what types of automation systems are utilized in support of B2B-sales and how they are applied throughout the various phases of the sales process. The thesis defines the characteristics of B2B sales and the sales process. The sales process is analyzed from both the sellers and customers perspectives. Based on the literature review, five main automation systems were identified. These systems are robotic process automation, artificial intelligence, customer relationship management systems, algorithms and chatbots. Based on the literature, different applications at different stages of the sales process were identified for automation systems. In the first stage of the sales process, automation systems were mainly used for lead identification and lead qualification. In the middle of the sales process, automation systems are used to support identifying customer needs, analytics, predictions and negotiations. In the final stages of the sales process, automation systems focus on closing deals, contract management, reporting and development of long customer relationships. sales.title: Salespeople's innovative behaviour: sustainable practices
sales.authors: María Badenas-Boldó, Gloria Berenguer Contrí, Irene Gil Saura
sales.abstract: Purpose Sustainability research has led to growing interest in the impacts of current production and consumption models, driven by greater awareness among companies and consumers. In this context, this paper aims to analyse the extent to which sustainable practices implemented in commercial distribution function as a strategic enabler of salespeople's innovative behaviour. It also examines the impact of sales-service ambidexterity on this relationship, as well as the importance of value co-creation. Design/methodology/approach The authors propose a theoretical model based on existing literature. This model was tested using partial least squares regression analysis (PLS-SEM) on a sample of 272 salespeople (business-to-business (B2B) and business-to-consumer (B2C)) from Spain and Portugal who work for a multinational building and decorating materials company. Findings The results show that sustainability dimensions are key factors driving salespeople's innovative service behaviour. Furthermore, sales-service ambidexterity and value co-creation significantly strengthen this relationship. As a result, these variables enhance the positive impact of sustainable practices on innovative behaviour. sales.title: Leveraging AI on Sales Management
sales.venue: Advances in computational intelligence and robotics book series
sales.abstract: Using data-driven tactics that improve decision-making, forecasting, and overall sales performance, this chapter examines how artificial intelligence (AI) confers authority onto sales management. In order to improve pipeline management, identify high-potential prospects, and design tailored outreach, sales managers may take use of the capabilities of artificial intelligence in the areas of predictive analytics, lead scoring, customer behavior analysis, and real-time insights respectively. With the use of artificial intelligence, workloads may be simplified by automating common processes and generating suggestions that can be implemented. This enables sales teams to concentrate on high-value activities and maximize win rates. In addition, coaching tools that are powered by artificial intelligence will assist managers in cultivating talent and enhancing the efficiency of their teams. By continually improving tactics based on emerging data patterns, integrating AI into sales management supports agility, precision, and sustained revenue development.

sales.title: Leveraging Network Marketing for B2B Sales: Strategies, Challenges, and Market Impact
sales.authors: Dr. Kamal Kishor Pandey, Dr. Himanshu Dargan, Dr. Rahul, Ms. Nidhi Varshney
sales.abstract: Network marketing is starting to make a name for itself in the business-to-business (B2B) sector, despite its more common association with consumer sales. In this article, we take a look at how network marketing helps companies increase their sales, strengthen their relationships, and broaden their reach in the market. Some of the tactics covered include multi-tiered distribution structures, referral-based sales, and digital marketing integration. Furthermore, the research highlights significant obstacles, such as trust concerns, regulatory limitations, and the intricacy of B2B decision-making. Surveys, interviews, and case studies of companies using network marketing for business-to-business transactions make up the study's mixed-method research methodology. The findings indicate that while network marketing can enhance sales performance and market reach, its success is contingent on credibility, technological support, & ethical practices. Companies that effectively navigate these challenges by leveraging digital tools and fostering transparency can gain a competitive advantage in the B2B landscape. In addition to providing useful advice for companies thinking about using network marketing to expand, this study adds to the expanding body of literature on alternate business-to-business sales models. sales.title: Use of Digital Tools for Sales Management in The Retail Business.
sales.venue: The American Journal of Management and Economics Innovations
sales.abstract: This article substantiates the necessity of transitioning to an integrated digital sales ecosystem as a key factor of competitiveness. The relevance of the study is determined by the rapid growth of electronic commerce and the approach of the online channel share to 20% in global retail, which renders traditional methods of sales management economically inefficient. The author emphasizes that digital transformation should be regarded not as a one-off project but as a continuously accelerating positive feedback loop requiring end-to-end integration of CRM, POS, BI, and ERP/OMS. The objective of the study is to systematize and analyze contemporary digital solutions applied to sales management in the retail business, as well as to identify the mechanisms of their interaction and their impact on key operational indicators. The methodological basis comprised a comparative analysis of reports by UNCTAD, Emarketer, McKinsey, Intellias, and leading industry research, as well as content analysis of practical case studies and statistical data. The theoretical part examines the four layers of the sales tech stack, while the empirical part provides examples of the implementation of AI modules, predictive analytics, and omnichannel platforms. sales.title: Leveraging AI for Go-To-Market Efficiency: A Framework for Product-Led Growth in B2B Sales Teams
sales.venue: International Journal on Science and Technology
sales.abstract: Product-led growth has emerged as a dominant model in B2B software, where users adopt products through self-service trials before engaging with sales teams. This shift creates challenges for traditional sales organizations that must identify high-value accounts, prioritize expansion opportunities, and personalize outreach based on product usage signals rather than manual research alone. This paper presents a practical framework for B2B sales teams adopting AI-assisted workflows in a product-led environment. We describe how usage data, firmographic enrichment, and language models combine to surface qualified accounts, generate contextual outreach, and support account planning. The framework covers signal identification, data integration patterns, AI-assisted messaging, and operational guardrails. While implementation examples reference common platforms, the approach remains portable to any stack with equivalent capabilities.

sales.title: Digital transformation of B2B sales in the souvenir industry: Ivan Valinchuk's original model
sales.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
sales.abstract: This manual is a comprehensive guide focused on the professional environment of the advertising and souvenir business, sales department heads, and e-commerce managers who seek to significantly improve the efficiency, scalability, and competitiveness of their business processes. sales.venue: Journal of the Association for Information Systems
sales.abstract: Digital feedback tools are increasingly relevant in the workplace, yet many recent advances lack features that genuinely enhance employee motivation, particularly in sales environments where individual performance directly shapes organizational outcomes. Drawing on goal-setting theory, this study investigates how self-set goals and adaptive, CRM-informed feedback influence salespeople’s performance in a B2B context. To this end, we propose a six-month field study within a B2B organization in which we enable employees to set, monitor, and adjust personal goals and provide them with data-driven feedback. With that, our research aims to contribute to the literature on goal setting, feedback, and motivational technologies in the workplace. Practically, our findings seek to guide organizations in designing IS-enabled interventions that enhance salesperson engagement and improve overall performance.
